title: Refugee self-reliance is constrained by the conversion gap between productive inputs, land, formal finance, documentation, and downstream markets
source_unit: UNHCR Uganda Refugee Response: Livelihoods and Resilience Dashboard, Quarter 2 2026, published September 2026
geography: Uganda refugee-hosting areas, including South Sudanese, Congolese, Sudanese, other refugee, and host-community populations

observations.period: January–June 2026; Uganda Refugee Response Plan livelihoods and resilience sector

denominator.unit: US dollars total 2026 funding requirement reported for the livelihoods and resilience sector

sector_pathway.value: productive assets and land, agricultural knowledge, producer organizations, markets, decent work, business services, financial inclusion, and market-aligned vocational training

observations.method: UNHCR operational dashboard compiled from partner ActivityInfo reporting; funding figures are preliminary and subject to validation.
observations.uncertainty: The dashboard reports programme outputs and funding status, not a complete response census, causal effect, beneficiary welfare trajectory, or final funding total.
observations.subgroup: Refugees and host communities in Uganda, humanitarian and development partners, agricultural households, workers, firms, and local authorities.
observations.counterinterpretation: A broad livelihood pathway can increase coordination while remaining too underfunded or fragmented to deliver durable self-reliance; partner reporting can overrepresent active locations and measurable activities.

denominator.unit: quarterly livelihood-output portfolio reported by the Uganda response

agricultural_inputs.unit: households receiving agricultural inputs and productive assets

good_agricultural_practices.unit: people trained on Good Agricultural Practices

observations.method: UNHCR dashboard output indicators with Q1-to-Q2 comparisons and partner reporting.
observations.uncertainty: Training, inputs, and linkages are not employment retention, income, profit, food security, or durable livelihood outcomes; indicators may overlap people or activities.
observations.subgroup: Refugee and host-community farmers, entrepreneurs, trainees, graduates, women, youth, employers, producer associations, and businesses.
observations.counterinterpretation: More training and linkages can increase aspirations without sufficient land, credit, buyers, legal status, or job demand; programme activity may intensify work without improving household room.

observations.period: Q2 2026; land constraint and self-reliance threshold

denominator.unit: households reported as accessing arable land

land_access.unit: acres of arable land accessed by refugees and host communities

average_land.unit: acres per supported household on average

critical_threshold.unit: acres per household identified as the critical minimum threshold for self-reliance

group_variation.value: South Sudanese households averaged 0.8 acres, Congolese 0.2, Sudanese 0.9, and host-community households 0.6

observations.method: UNHCR dashboard land-access indicators and sector narrative comparing average access with a stated self-reliance threshold.
observations.uncertainty: The threshold is a programme planning benchmark, not a universal causal minimum; land quality, crop choice, household size, markets, climate, and nonfarm income are not captured by acres alone.
observations.subgroup: South Sudanese, Congolese, Sudanese, other refugee, and host-community households with different land access and livelihood conditions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Households can pursue nonfarm livelihoods or intensive production on smaller plots, while more land may not generate income without inputs, water, storage, buyers, security, and rights.

observations.period: Q2 2026; formalization, financial inclusion, and documentation barriers

vsla_formation.unit: village savings and loan associations formed

barriers.value: refugee documentation, Know Your Customer requirements, limited formal credit, and access to formal employment restrict economic opportunities

digital_route.value: safe digital and banking services and stronger financial inclusion are identified as priorities

observations.method: UNHCR operational dashboard and sector narrative linking outputs with formalization and documentation constraints.
observations.uncertainty: Formal registration and savings-group formation do not establish business survival, credit access, profitability, wage quality, or equal refugee-host participation.
observations.subgroup: Refugee entrepreneurs, host-community businesses, women participating in savings groups, workers, banks, employers, and people facing documentation or KYC barriers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Formalization and digital finance can improve visibility and access but may also impose fees, surveillance, identity barriers, repayment risk, or exclusion for people with precarious legal status.

related_sources.claim: UNHCR Uganda Operational Data Portal country context.
Direct PDF dashboard download used for the reported Q2 indicators.

boundary: This record adds an operational refugee-livelihood route linking land, inputs, skills, producer organizations, market access, formalization, finance, documentation, and self-reliance. It is a partner-reporting dashboard with preliminary funding data, not a representative household panel, causal programme evaluation, or proof of sustained income, employment, food security, or durable refugee-host integration.
